info.title: The Desk ↔ server contract
info.description: Every message between a Desk core and the Gentility server, named by domain, not by topic. Hand-kept: change it, then the server, and record the exchange. A method's `x-refusals` are the closed words it may refuse with, besides `x-common-refusals`; `x-phoenix` is where it lives on the Phoenix channel framing; `x-feature` is the hello word that gates it. A method or notification marked `x-untyped` carries its words and no shapes yet. The rules, and how the recorded exchanges are held to this, are in README.md beside it.

methods.name: door.open
methods.description: A Desk core declaring its door, the `port` it listens on at the 6net `address`, as the `desk` service on its own node (`Gentility.Sessions.Door.open/4`): a person's core on a node the person owns, a bound host on its machine's. Said each time the listener opens, and idempotent. `approved` says whether the service is; a port another live service holds is `port_taken`.

schema.description: The 6net address the door listens on.

methods.name: door.peer
methods.description: Who owns the 6net `address` dialling a Desk core's door (`Gentility.Sessions.Door.person/2`). An address another organization holds is `unknown_peer`, as is one nobody holds.

user_id.description: The person who owns the node; null for a machine's.

methods.name: door.withdraw
methods.description: The inverse of `door.open`, said as the core stops (`Gentility.Sessions.Door.withdraw/4`): the same `address` and `port`, answered with whether a live door was there to withdraw. A person's core withdraws on a node the person owns and no other (`not_your_machine`); a port another kind holds is `kind_mismatch`.

schema.description: The 6net address the door listens on.

methods.name: grants.delegate
methods.description: A thread passes on its person's grant over one thread to a thread it manages, or withdraws one it passed on (T-584, `Gentility.Desk.Grants.delegate/2`), written as a `thread_management_grant` fact on the grantee's session that names the delegator in `by.session_id` and the person's decision it rests on in `basis`, idempotent on `op_id`. The person's connection asks it for the delegator, which the core holds to the calling thread. The grant reaches `session:<target>` alone, for 24 hours when `expires_at` is null, never more than 168 hours or past the grant it rests on; the answer gives the expiry that stands. Refused `delegation_refused` for a party twice or another person's, or where the person has withdrawn this grant, `not_your_child` where the grantee's manager is not the delegator, `already_granted` where the person's own grant stands, `management_grant_required` where the delegator holds no grant of the person's own over the target or its organization, `not_delegated_by_you` for a withdrawal of a grant the delegator did not pass on; a bound host or an agent is `forbidden`, as is a blank or absent `reason` or an `expires_at` already past.

schema.description: The thread passing its grant on, a UUID.
The thread it passes the grant to, a UUID: one the delegator manages.
The one thread the grant reaches, a UUID.
A UUID; the grant's idempotency key. The server mints one when it is null.
An ISO 8601 instant; null for 24 hours from now.
Why, at most 4096 bytes, shown to the person.

row_seq.description: The organization's row cursor once the grant is written.

expires_at.description: The expiry that stands; null on a withdrawal.

methods.name: grants.set
methods.description: A person's grant to one of their threads, or its withdrawal (`Gentility.Desk.Grants.set/5`), written as a `thread_management_grant` fact on the grantee's session and idempotent on `op_id`. `scope` is `session:<id>`, a session the person may write, or `organization:<id>`, the lobby's own; `on` says whether the thread holds it. The answer is the organization's `row_seq` once the grant is written, which the core waits for its feed to reach. A person's alone: a bound host, an agent or one acting as another is `forbidden`, as are an `expires_at` already past on a grant turned on and a blank `reason`; a grantee the person may not write is `not_found`.

schema.description: The thread granted, a UUID.
`session:<id>` or `organization:<id>`.
A UUID; the grant's idempotency key. The server mints one when it is null.
An ISO 8601 instant; null for a grant with no clock.
What the person said, at most 4096 bytes; null is `chosen by the person`.

row_seq.description: The organization's row cursor once the grant is written.

methods.name: groups.convene
methods.description: Convenes a group from the person's Desk (`Gentility.AgentGroups.convene/3`): 2 to 6 new threads answering one question, on the person's own Desk machines. The connection's machine, the one its hello named, is the convener's: members that name no machine start there, and the operation key `op` is bound to the person and that machine, so a retry with it answers the same group and starts nothing. Answers at once, with each member's start as it stands. Only Desk's own sign-in convenes. A refusal of the group's is `invalid`, with its sentence. Served only on `/desk/rpc`, under `rpc_groups`, with no Phoenix handler: a core on a link without it refuses the call itself, at once.

label.description: A, B, … when absent; at most 40 characters, no quotation marks or line breaks.

machine.description: One of the person's Desk machines, by label or id; this Desk when absent.

schema.description: The label of the member who writes the closing summary.

status.description: `running`, `summarising` (its chair writes the closing summary) or `ended`.

reason.description: `failed`: the start's refusal, in one word.

methods.name: groups.get
methods.description: One group of the organization as a person reads it (`Gentility.AgentGroups.read/3`): its question, members and their state, up to 50 posts after the number `after`, and its header's `progress` in words and `convened_at`. Anyone in the organization reads. Served only on `/desk/rpc`, under `rpc_groups`, with no Phoenix handler: a core on a link without it refuses the call itself, at once.

schema.description: Posts after this number; 0 when absent.

methods.name: groups.list
methods.description: A page of the organization's groups, newest first by when each was convened (`Gentility.AgentGroups.list/2`). `limit` is 1 to 50, 50 when absent; `cursor` is a page's `next_cursor`, opaque. Any other key, a limit out of bounds or a cursor the server did not give is `malformed_payload`, with its sentence. Anyone in the organization reads. Served only on `/desk/rpc`, under `rpc_groups`, with no Phoenix handler: a core on a link without it refuses the call itself, at once.

schema.description: A previous page's `next_cursor`.

next_cursor.description: The next page's cursor; null on the last page.

methods.name: groups.stop
methods.description: Stops a group (`Gentility.AgentGroups.stop/2`): the person who convened it, or an organization admin. A running group's open turns end and its chair, if any, writes the summary (`summarising`); a second stop ends it at once. Only Desk's own sign-in stops. A stop is not idempotent, so a task that dies answers `outcome_unknown`. Served only on `/desk/rpc`, under `rpc_groups`, with no Phoenix handler: a core on a link without it refuses the call itself, at once.

status.description: `running`, `summarising` (its chair writes the closing summary) or `ended`.

methods.name: hosts.bind_code
methods.description: A one-time code to bind a Desk host to the organization machine `machine_id` (`Gentility.Sessions.Bindings.mint_code/2`), good for five minutes and spent once. An admin's of that machine alone, as `Gentility.Access.check/3` decides.

schema.description: The organization machine, a UUID.

methods.name: hosts.list
methods.description: The Hosts list (`Gentility.Sessions.Bindings.hosts/2`): the organization's machines the caller holds a role on, every one for an owner or admin, and the caller's own Desk installs that opened a door on a node granted here, `kind` saying which. A bound host is listed every machine and no install. Each row says its node's presence and door, its Desk registration, who holds which role on it and the caller's own. A personal row names its install by `store_id`, and has no `machine_id`, `slug` or holders.

machine_id.description: The organization machine; null on a personal row.

store_id.description: A personal row's alone: its Desk install's store id.

label.description: An organization machine's hostname, or its slug; a personal install's label.

slug.description: The organization machine's slug; null on a personal row.

node.description: The machine's 6net node, null for a machine with none granted here.

address.description: This organization's address for the node.

presence.description: `direct`, `relayed` or `offline`; a node with no presence row is `offline`.

door_port.description: The port of the node's approved `desk` service, null while it has none.

reachable.description: Whether the overlay lets the asking install's own node reach the row's approved door; null when the asker has no node, false for a row with no node or door.

desk.description: The Desk on the machine, null for a machine no Desk is bound to. `incarnation`, `os`, `arch` and `account` are what a bound host said of itself at its last connect.

live.description: Whether the install holds its desk channel now.

generation.description: What the server fences a bound host's writes by.

registered_at.description: When the binding was made; null for an install no binding made.

holders.description: One entry per live relation on the machine, highest role first.

name.description: A user's full name or email; a group's name.

role.description: The caller's highest role: `admin`, `operator` or `viewer` on an organization machine, `owner` on a personal install; null for a bound host, and for an admin listed a machine they hold no role on.

methods.name: hosts.machines
methods.description: The organization's machines on 6net (`Gentility.Overlay.machines/1`), one for each node holding an active grant here, and when each was last heard. Each comes with the Desk machine it is, if any, and the server's `now`. The address and label are this organization's alone.

name.description: A user's email, a machine's slug, a runtime's sprite name; null when that record is gone.

address.description: This organization's address for the node: the one to dial it on here.

path.description: `direct`, `relayed` or `offline`. Presence is not a fact: a node with no presence row is `offline`, never heard.

state.description: The service's status, never `removed`: a removed service is not listed.

desk_machine_id.description: The first linked Desk install in desk_installs, or null when none is linked. Older servers omit desk_installs and expose only this identity.

desk_presence.description: Linked Desk presence: online or offline; null when no Desk is linked. Missing, null or unknown values mean no Desk evidence. A clean socket close marks offline immediately; otherwise it can lag by about 150 seconds (heartbeat timeout plus sweep).

desk_installs.description: Linked installs, ordered by approved door port in this organization (nulls last), then id. Legacy single fields equal the first entry. IPv4 remains per node.

ipv4.description: The node's private IPv4 addresses from its latest network report, RFC 1918 only, physical interfaces first and virtual ones only when it reported no physical one; empty when unreported. Desk's menu bar offers each to copy.

methods.name: hosts.token
methods.description: The delegation token a window carries to the host bound to the organization machine `machine_id`, naming the person and the Desk `client` they are on (`Gentility.Sessions.Delegation.mint/3`), good for ten minutes. A machine no host is bound to is `not_bound`.

schema.description: The organization machine, a UUID.
The Desk client the person is on.

token.description: A compact JWS under the organization's key.

scope.description: What the person's role on the machine gives: `operate` for an operator or an admin, `view` for a viewer.

methods.name: inbox.command
methods.description: One inbox command on one session's row (`Gentility.Sessions.Inbox.command/6`): each field in `changes` is written last-writer-wins at `at`, and a field a later write already holds is `stale`, which the row snaps back to. A repeated `op_id` keeps its first outcome. `row_seq` is the organization's row cursor once it is applied, so a reader knows when its feed has caught up. `by` describes the actor (`person`, `agent` or `desk`, and the session that acts). A read is always the authenticated person's.

schema.description: A UUID; the command's idempotency key.
An ISO 8601 instant.
Fields of the row: `settled_at`, `snoozed_until`, `archived_at`, `rank`, `title`, `read_at`, `waiting_on`, `waiting_reason`.
The person a bound host acts for.

methods.name: lobby.join
methods.description: The join of `work_sessions:<org>`: the core's hello, answered with the server's feature words and what this organization's desks work under. `claude_route` is true while the organization's inference route has its Claude switch on, whatever the gateway's state (`Gentility.Sessions.ClaudeRoutes.routed?/1`): a core asks `lobby.claude_route` only for an organization it last heard true, failing the start closed if that is refused, and otherwise starts Claude on the person's own login at once, offline too. Every rejoin answers it afresh.

methods.name: loopers.feed
methods.description: The board since the reader's cursor (`CloudLoop.Board.page/4`): the runs and the reader's own loopers stamped past `since`, the ids gone from each, and the cursor to ask from next. `reset` sends the reader back to zero. A request on a feed row carries no `can_grant` or `missing`.

methods.name: loopers.history
methods.description: One looper's runs, newest first, at most 50, in the rows `loopers.list_runs` sends.

methods.name: loopers.join
methods.description: The Phoenix framing's join of `looper_threads:<org>`: the core's hello, answered with the server's feature words. It goes with that framing; on `/desk/rpc` the connection's `hello` says the same.

methods.name: loopers.list_owned
methods.description: The loopers this member owns (`CloudLoop.list_owned_loopers/1`), for a desk to pin above its threads. Reads no params.

methods.name: loopers.list_runs
methods.description: The organization's looper runs that have something to say (`CloudLoop.list_thread_runs/2`): the sidebar's run rows. Reads no params.

methods.name: loopers.read_run
methods.description: One run as a thread: its header, its turns behind the run page's private gate, and every request it raised, oldest first.

methods.name: loopers.resolve_request
methods.description: Resolves one request with `decision`, in the shape the MCP tool sends (`Requests.Decision.from_args/1`). Answered now or refused now, never held. `Decision.refusal/1` words any atom as itself, so this is the one open vocabulary: the list is what `Requests.resolve/3` and the kinds' grants return today.

methods.name: loopers.run_now
methods.description: Wakes an owned looper now (`CloudLoop.run_owned_looper_now/3`). With a `message`, the person's words are the run's first turn, a chat (`CloudLoop.Chat.open/4`), and `message_id` is the id the client minted for them, so a send repeated after a lost answer is answered from the first; with none, or null, it is the page's Run now. The run's row reaches the desk on the next `loopers.changed`.

methods.name: loopers.say
methods.description: A person's reply on a finished run of a looper they own (`CloudLoop.Chat.say/4`): the run carries on with one more turn, numbered `turn`. `message_id` is the id the client minted for the person's words, so a reply repeated after a lost answer is answered from the first. An older server answers `unknown_event`. The run's row reaches the desk on the next `loopers.changed`.

methods.name: loopers.update
methods.description: An edit of an owned looper: `changes` are the settings its web page lets a person change (`CloudLoop.update_owned_looper/3`). The row comes back as `loopers.list_owned` lists it.

methods.name: machine.answer
methods.description: Answers a `phone_claim` ask. `wrong_number` is the `reason` of an ok reply that denied the claim, not a refusal.

schema.description: The two digits the redeeming phone shows; an `allow` without them, or with others, denies the claim.

status.description: The claim's status after the answer: `allowed` or `denied`, or another the claim reached first. A reader passes a word it does not know through.

reason.description: Only `wrong_number`, on a denial the server made for a missing or wrong number.

methods.name: machine.fact
methods.description: Facts about the machine, a batch at a time (`Gentility.Desk.record/3`). A fact whose `client_seq` is at or below the highest the machine's ledger holds is a replay after a lost reply, dropped and acknowledged: `seq` is the last fact appended, null when none was, and `last_client_seq` the highest `client_seq` held, null when none is. An `ask_answered` fact is how the core answers a `machine.ask`.

client_seq.description: Strictly increasing per machine, not dense.

methods.name: machine.heartbeat
methods.description: Re-arms the machine's presence (`Gentility.Desk.MachinePresence`); a core sends one every 30 seconds.

methods.name: machine.join
methods.description: The Phoenix framing's join of `desk:<org>:<machine>`: the core's hello, answered with the socket's person, null for a bound host. It holds the machine live (`Gentility.Desk.Live`) while it lasts. On `/desk/rpc` the connection's `hello` says the same. A person's join of a closed organization is `unauthorized`, the membership's word, which the close made true: a core files the machine under the login's next organization on it, so the person's other organizations go on hearing the machine, and after a reopen the machine stays where it moved, which carries it for the reopened organization too. A bound host, which is never moved, is told `organization_closed`, which it asks again after, and it joins again once the organization is reopened. Session topics say `organization_closed` to a person too, which is not final.

methods.name: machine.phone_claim_mint
methods.description: Mints the QR a phone scans (`Gentility.Phone.mint_claim/2`), from a person's Desk sign-in only. The code rides in `url`'s fragment.

methods.name: machine.presence
methods.description: Whether the person is at this Desk, held while the connection lives (`Gentility.Desk.Presence`) and read before a phone is buzzed. `session_id` comes with `watching` only, and always.

methods.name: machine.screenshot_accept
methods.description: Fresh screenshot verdict for an authenticated org-bound install. Personal bearer connections are refused. Requires end-to-end verified TLS; no tool is offered before endpoint proof.

methods.name: mcp.list
methods.description: The MCP servers the person sees in one project, or everywhere when `project` is null (`Gentility.MCP.Upstreams.for_desk/2`): the organization's and their own, never another member's, that are offered there. Each says its `level`, the project it is limited to, its `state`, how many tools it has, and the person's switches: `on`, not switched off everywhere, and `on_here`, not switched off in `project` either (equal to `on` when it is null). A project that does not read as one is `invalid_project`, with the context's sentence.

schema.description: A remote or a project key; null for everywhere.

level.description: `org` for the organization's, `user` for the person's own.

project_key.description: The one project it is offered in; null for all.

methods.name: mcp.switch
methods.description: Switches one MCP server on or off for the person (`Gentility.MCP.Upstreams.switch/4`), in one project, or everywhere when `project` is null, which governs their loopers too. Switching the same way twice changes nothing. A server limited to one project switches only there or everywhere (`project_mismatch`). Each refusal carries the context's sentence.

schema.description: A remote or a project key; null for everywhere.

methods.name: models.claude_route
methods.description: A session's Claude Code route through the organization's model gateway (`Gentility.Sessions.ClaudeRoutes`). `route` is null while the organization has no inference route or its Claude switch is off: Claude starts on the person's own login. Otherwise it is a key minted for this session alone, and `base_url` is the gateway's origin with no `/v1`. A refusal's `message` names the switch in organization settings; a Desk fails the start closed on either word.

methods.name: models.codex_route
methods.description: The organization's inference route for Codex, resolved afresh (`Gentility.Sessions.InferenceRoutes.resolve_for/2`). `route` is null while the organization has no route or no service on it, or its Codex switch is off: Codex starts on the person's own login. Otherwise it names the route and the 6net service serving it, `base_url` is the gateway with `/v1`, and `bearer` is the organization's access key for the gateway, a secret the core keeps out of every log and inspector. Every failure, a service not selectable now included, is `route_unavailable`, and a core fails Codex's start closed on it. No payload is read.

methods.name: models.list
methods.description: Which models a Desk may offer, per harness (`Gentility.Sessions.Models.for_desk/2`). Claude's and Codex's are every name the server has seen and priced, in name order; a name seen and not priced is not listed, and a core reads an absent name as unpriced. oh-my-pi's is its grant (`Gentility.Sessions.OmpRoutes.access/1`): the gateway's offer in its own order, or `refused`, the word for why there is none. A row carries its name and `priced` and, for Claude and Codex, each row's `legacy` and `new` marks as the server derives them. Claude and Codex rows also carry an optional spec_id. For aliases it is withheld while the latest label change is newer than the latest decision; price and marks remain during that interval. A name the catalog prices directly always carries its code, whatever its label.

priced.description: Always true: a name the server does not price is not listed.

legacy.description: The server's word that the model is superseded, deprecated or retired: a core that reads it draws the row under Legacy. Absent from an older server, which leaves the bundled catalog to say.

new.description: Released within the last 42 days, as the server reads the catalog; never true with `legacy`. Absent from an older server.

spec_id.description: The model's catalog code. Omitted for aliases after a label change until a later decision, and by older servers. Catalog-priced full names always carry their code.

priced.description: Always true: a name the server does not price is not listed.

legacy.description: The server's word that the model is superseded, deprecated or retired: a core that reads it draws the row under Legacy. Absent from an older server, which leaves the bundled catalog to say.

new.description: Released within the last 42 days, as the server reads the catalog; never true with `legacy`. Absent from an older server.

spec_id.description: The model's catalog code. Omitted for aliases after a label change until a later decision, and by older servers. Catalog-priced full names always carry their code.

omp.description: Exactly one of `models`, the priced names, or `refused`, why there are none.

priced.description: Always true: a name the server does not price is not listed.

methods.name: models.omp_access
methods.description: Whether the organization would grant oh-my-pi a route, and the models it would offer, each priced, in the gateway's order (`Gentility.Sessions.OmpRoutes.access/1`). Mints nothing. `no_gateway` is no Desk gateway that can serve them, `no_credit` an organization with no credit, each with a sentence; anything else is `route_unavailable`.

methods.name: models.omp_route
methods.description: A fresh oh-my-pi key for one session on the organization's Desk gateway (`Gentility.Sessions.OmpRoutes.grant/2`). It revokes the session's earlier key, and is handed out only once the gateway accepts it. `token` is a bearer secret for the omp process's environment alone, never written or logged; `base_url` is the gateway's, with `/v1`, and `models` what the key may use. A closed session, or one this organization does not hold, is `route_unavailable`, as is every failure but `no_gateway` and `no_credit`.

methods.name: models.seen
methods.description: The models a Desk agent advertised for one harness, so the server learns and prices every model Desk sees (`Gentility.Sessions.Models.see/4`); the socket's Desk install is the reporter. A name already known appends nothing, and a `default` row names no model. A list it cannot read is `invalid` and appends nothing: a harness other than `claude`, `codex` or `omp`, more than 200 rows, a row without a string `value`, an empty or overlong name or label.

methods.name: phone.devices
methods.description: The person's phones that are not revoked, for Settings.

methods.name: phone.join
methods.description: The join of `phone:<user>`, a person's phones, by that person's own socket and nobody else's. It is bound to no organization, because a phone is the person's across all of theirs.

methods.name: phone.mute
methods.description: Silences one row on every one of the person's phones, or lets it speak again (`Gentility.Phone.set_mute/4`). The row is named by exactly one of `session_id` or `looper_id`.

methods.name: phone.mutes
methods.description: The rows silenced on every one of the person's phones, by kind.

methods.name: phone.register
methods.description: What the phone sends after sign-in and on every launch (`Gentility.Phone.register_device/2`): its name, its platform, its push token, and the APNs environment its build was signed for. Anything else is `malformed_payload`. The push token is opaque and never logged.

schema.description: The claim this phone was enrolled by, a UUID.
`sandbox` or `production`.

methods.name: phone.revoke
methods.description: Ends one of the person's phones (`Gentility.Phone.revoke_device/2`): its bearer and node, then the socket that bearer holds open. A phone revoking itself may lose this reply to the disconnect, and takes a closed socket after `revoke` as done. A phone that is not the person's is `unknown`.

schema.description: A UUID.

methods.name: projects.list
methods.description: Organization reference data the lobby serves, though it is not about sessions: the Architecture Manager's ruled exception (T-169). The organization's active projects, by slug (`Gentility.Projects.real/1`), each with its repositories as `owner/name`, sorted; an archived project is absent. No payload is read. The lobby pushes `projects_changed` when one moves.

methods.name: projects.repositories
methods.description: Organization reference data the lobby serves, though it is not about sessions. The repositories a desk may offer to clone (`Gentility.Sessions.repositories/1`): those of the organization's active GitHub installations, one a name case aside, in name order. An organization with none answers an empty list. No payload is read. `default_branch` is null where the installation's cache does not know it.

methods.name: pulls.comment
methods.description: A session's agent speaking on its pull request's conversation as the organization's GitHub App, never as the person (`Gentility.Sessions.PullRequestSpeech.speak/5`), recorded as a quiet `pr_commented` fact. The pull request is the session's one open link (`no_pull_request` for none, `ambiguous_pull_request` for two), or the linked one `number` names whatever became of it (`no_such_link` for one it is not linked to). Not idempotent: each ask posts once, and `unrecorded` is words GitHub took that no session records, not to be posted again. RPC-only unavailable means the per-connection write bound was reached before GitHub was asked. RPC-only outcome_unknown means the task died and GitHub may have acted; check the pull request before asking again. Neither is retried or replayed.

schema.description: The words to post. Blank, or longer than 65,536 characters, is refused before GitHub is asked.
The linked pull request to post on, whatever became of it; absent or null for the session's one open link.

methods.name: pulls.list
methods.description: A repository's fifty most recently updated open pull requests, asked of GitHub live through the organization's installation that lists it, and stored nowhere (`Gentility.Sessions.pull_requests/3`). `full_name` is `owner/name`, matched case aside; `more` says GitHub holds more. `not_connected` is no active installation of this organization listing the repository, and `unavailable` GitHub not answering. Answered from a task, so a slow GitHub holds up no other push.

author.description: The author's login; null for an account GitHub no longer knows.

head.description: The branch it would merge from.

methods.name: pulls.open
methods.description: Opens the session's pull request on GitHub as the organization's App, and records it as `pr_opened` (`Gentility.Sessions.PullRequests.open/4`). `head` is the branch the desk has just pushed; `base`, sent only when origin has it, is the branch to merge into, else the repository's default. Idempotent: a session whose row already answers for `head` is answered off the row, and GitHub is not asked. The answer's `head` is the branch the answered pull request was opened from, null for a row that does not know it, and `url` is null only for a row whose link recorded none; `repo` is `owner/name` as the session's remote reads now. Each refusal carries a sentence for the person (`GentilityWeb.WorkSessionsChannel.pr_refusal/1`); `internal` is the pull request opened and not recorded, and asking again records it. RPC-only unavailable means the per-connection write bound was reached before GitHub was asked. RPC-only outcome_unknown means the task died and GitHub may have acted; check the pull request before asking again. Neither is retried or replayed.

schema.description: Not empty.
Not empty.

methods.name: pulls.reply
methods.description: A reply in a review comment's thread on the session's pull request (`Gentility.Sessions.PullRequestSpeech.speak/5`), spoken as `pr_comment` is. RPC-only unavailable means the per-connection write bound was reached before GitHub was asked. RPC-only outcome_unknown means the task died and GitHub may have acted; check the pull request before asking again. Neither is retried or replayed.

schema.description: The words to post. Blank, or longer than 65,536 characters, is refused before GitHub is asked.
GitHub's id for the review comment whose thread is replied in.
The linked pull request to post on, whatever became of it; absent or null for the session's one open link.

methods.name: pulls.review
methods.description: A review of event `COMMENT` on the session's pull request (`Gentility.Sessions.PullRequestSpeech.speak/5`), spoken as `pr_comment` is: `body`, and at most 50 line comments on the new version of the files. The event is the server's and never the ask's: a thread does not approve, or request changes on, its own pull request. RPC-only unavailable means the per-connection write bound was reached before GitHub was asked. RPC-only outcome_unknown means the task died and GitHub may have acted; check the pull request before asking again. Neither is retried or replayed.

schema.description: The words to post. Blank, or longer than 65,536 characters, is refused before GitHub is asked.
The linked pull request to post on, whatever became of it; absent or null for the session's one open link.
Line comments; anything else in one is not read.

start_line.description: The first line of a range.

methods.name: pulls.unlink
methods.description: Takes one pull request out of a session's set, by its repository as `owner/name` and its number (`Gentility.Sessions.PullRequests.unlink/4`). The `pr_unlinked` it appends is a tombstone the matcher reads, so the pull request is never linked to this session again; a link the session does not hold, or no longer does, is `no_such_link`.

schema.description: Not empty.

methods.name: questions.answer
methods.description: Accepts an open question with `value`, the answer to its form (`Gentility.Sessions.Questions.Person.answer/3`). A question the server holds is answered at once, `answered` with the `answer` recorded. One waiting on its thread is asked of the thread's machine: `answered` once it took the answer, or `pending` with the `ask_id` while it has not said. An answer that does not fit the form is `malformed_payload` with `errors`; one already given is `already_decided`, with the recorded `answer` where there is one. Any other key is `malformed_payload`. Only the person, on a socket that may write sessions, for a session they may write (`forbidden` otherwise); at most four writes at once a socket (`unavailable` past that).

ask_id.description: `pending`: the ask the thread's machine has not yet answered.

answer.description: `answered`, for a question the server holds: the answer recorded.

methods.name: questions.dismiss
methods.description: Dismisses a question (`Gentility.Sessions.Questions.Person.dismiss/3`). One the server holds is cancelled, with `reason` if given, 1 to 500 bytes. One waiting on its thread is declined there, takes no `reason`, and may answer `pending` with the `ask_id` as `question_answer` does. A question already declined or cancelled is `dismissed` again; one already answered is `already_decided`, with the recorded `answer`. Any other key is `malformed_payload`. Bounded as `question_answer` is.

ask_id.description: `pending`: the ask the thread's machine has not yet answered.

methods.name: questions.list
methods.description: A page of the person's addressed questions in this organization (`Gentility.Sessions.Questions.Person.list/2`): `open` ones, the default, oldest first, or `closed` ones of the last seven days, newest first. `limit` is 1 to 100, 50 when absent; `cursor` is a page's `next_cursor`, for the same section. Any other key is `malformed_payload`. `open_count` and `open_session_ids` are of every open question, and `closed_count` of every closed one of the last seven days, not the page's alone, read in one snapshot with it; `starts_at` is when the server began recording questions. The person's own socket only: anyone else is `forbidden`. Answered from a task, at most four reads at once a socket (`unavailable` past that).

answerable.description: Whether the person can answer it here: it has a form the window can draw.

joined_count.description: How many of the person's other threads joined it.

thread_title.description: The asking thread's title, or `Untitled thread`.

parked.description: Whether it waits on its thread's machine, which answers it.

holder_online.description: Whether the machine holding the thread is a Desk that is online.

form.description: The form to answer with, an elicitation's requested schema as `Gentility.Elicitation.validate_schema/1` keeps it; absent for a question that cannot be answered here. A JSON Schema, open because it is the asker's.

about.description: What the asker said it is about: a task number, a pull request, or both.

project.description: The thread's project, or just its repository's name, `id` absent, when no active project holds it.

machine.description: The machine the thread is placed on.

manager.description: The person's thread that manages the asking one.

ended_at.description: When it ended or expired; present on every question that is not `open`.

ended_by.description: Who ended it, where the server knows; a decline is the person's, shown as `you`.

kind.description: `person`, `session`, `server`, or the word the ending fact said.

reason.description: A cancelled question's reason, where it was given one.

open_session_ids.description: Every thread with an open question, by id.

now.description: The server's clock as it read the page.

methods.name: refusals.allow
methods.description: An Allow of one refused edge, through the website's authorization and ledger operation (`GentilityWeb.RefusalReview.allow/3`): `all_my_machines` between two of the person's own machines, with no clock, or `this_machine` until `expires_in` from now, over `kind`. A choice that does not parse is `invalid_choice`. A port a withdrawn service keeps is `port_taken`, with the `message` a person reads naming the machine.

schema.description: A refusal's id.
`1d`, `7d`, `30d` or `365d`; `this_machine` needs it, and `all_my_machines` ignores it.

opened.description: `now`, or `on_approval` for a service still waiting on an admin.

kind.description: The kind of the service the Allow landed on, which may be one already on the port rather than the one picked.

methods.name: refusals.list
methods.description: The refused 6net edges this person owns an end of, or every one for a manager of the organization, that no live path opens and the person has not muted (`Gentility.Overlay.refused_edges/1`), newest first, with the server's `now`. An edge is its attempts grouped by source, destination, protocol and port; its `id` and `reason` are its latest attempt's.

id.description: The latest attempt's id, which `refusals.review`, `refusals.allow` and the mutes take.

source.description: The source machine's 6net label in this organization.

destination.description: The destination machine's 6net label in this organization.

can_allow.description: Whether this person may allow it: a manager, or the destination's owner, and never into a withdrawn Desk door's port.

methods.name: refusals.mute
methods.description: Stops listing one refused edge to this person, by a refusal's `id` (`Gentility.Overlay.mute_refusal/2`). Idempotent. An edge the person may not see is `not_found`; one whose end machine has left 6net is `machine_gone`.

schema.description: A refusal's id.

methods.name: refusals.review
methods.description: The Allow page's reading of one refused edge (`GentilityWeb.RefusalReview.read/2`): its ends, the live service on its port and the one withdrawn from it, the kinds an Allow may declare there and the one proposed, the expiries offered and the path that already opens it. A withdrawn `desk` is a Desk that is offline, which no Allow reopens: `kinds` is empty and `can_allow` false.

schema.description: A refusal's id.

name.description: The machine's 6net label in this organization.
The machine's 6net label in this organization.

same_owner.description: Whether one person owns both machines, so `all_my_machines` is the reach to offer.

owner_name.description: The destination's owner, by full name or else email; null for a machine no person owns.

service.description: The live service on the port, null for none.

withdrawn.description: The service the port held before it was withdrawn, when it holds no live one; null otherwise.

kinds.description: The kinds an Allow may declare here: of `api`, `ssh` and `desk`.

proposed_kind.description: The kind to offer first, null when `kinds` is empty.

open.description: The live path that already opens the edge, null for none.

until.description: When the latest live path lapses; null for one with no clock.

methods.name: refusals.unmute
methods.description: Lists one refused edge to this person again (`Gentility.Overlay.unmute_refusal/2`): `refusals.mute`'s inverse, as idempotent and refused in the same words.

schema.description: A refusal's id.

methods.name: rpc.hello
methods.description: The first request on `/desk/rpc`, and the only one served before it: the core's hello (`GentilityWeb.DeskHello`) and, for a bound host, the generation it holds, fenced here as a connect was (`Bindings.fence/2`); a person's Desk names its machine, and the os and arch of the box it runs on, to be registered (`Machines.register/4`); a Desk too old to say them leaves the install's unknown. Answers who the credential is, the server's feature words, and the organizations it reaches. Said once. A host whose organization closed since the upgrade gets no answer: the connection closes 1013 (`x-rpc`'s `close`), because a refused hello stops a core for good.

methods.name: rpc.unwatch
methods.description: Stop hearing `org`'s streams. Unwatching what is not watched is no error.

methods.name: rpc.watch
methods.description: Hear `org`'s streams as notifications carrying `org`, answering the cursor of each stream that has one, so a core pulls from there. `loopers` is `loopers.changed`, with its cursor. `machine` is what joining `desk:<org>:<machine>` was: the connection holds its machine live until it unwatches its last organization or closes, `machine.heartbeat` re-arms its deadline, and `machine.ask` is pushed for every ask still open, then for each one raised; it has no cursor, and a connection whose hello named no machine is refused `forbidden`. Joining a topic did this on the Phoenix framing. The sessions stream emits sessions.changed; its authoritative cursor and generation come from sessions.feed, so this watch adds no cursor. Watch first, then call sessions.feed from the stored cursor and page until more is false; changes before the watch are caught by the feed, and changes after it also emit sessions.changed. The groups stream emits groups.changed, with the group's id, and has no cursor; only a person's Desk watches it, and a bound host, which is no person, is refused `forbidden`.

methods.name: session.append
methods.description: One session's facts, a batch at a time, in client order (`Gentility.Sessions.append/4`), from the machine that holds it. `client_seq` is dense per session: a fact at or below the highest held is a replay, taken as nothing new only if it is the fact held there (`replay_mismatch` otherwise), and the first new one must be exactly one past it (`sequence_gap` names the one expected). The answer is the highest `client_seq` the server now holds; a batch is acked up to there and no further. A core that holds the lease says its `epoch`; one that does not is told `stale_epoch`, or `not_a_holder` when its hello named no lease support. A bound host's batch is fenced by its binding's generation first (`superseded`). A transcript item the server's copy cannot place refuses the batch, naming the `item`: a message whose role changed (`invalid_role`), or an item naming a message the copy does not hold (`unknown_message`). A later server may place it, so the core keeps the queue and waits. At most fifty facts a batch.

actor.description: The person a bound host acted for, a member of the session's organization (`unknown_actor` otherwise).

schema.description: The lease epoch the core holds the session at.

last_client_seq.description: The highest `client_seq` the server holds for the session.

methods.name: session.brief
methods.description: The scoped session's exact binding-rendered brief body. Empty params; the session comes from the channel or RPC scope. Checks rendered_sha256 before answering; a missing pinned skill or other render drift is pin_mismatch, never a partial body. At most 65536 UTF-8 bytes. A read with no retry or replay; RPC task death is unavailable.

methods.name: session.join
methods.description: The Phoenix framing's join of `work_session:<session>`, from Desk only (`forbidden` to any other client) and only for a session the socket may read. A session that does not exist and one this socket may not read are both `unauthorized`, so naming a session says nothing of whether it exists. A bound host whose binding moved on is `superseded`. A session of a closed organization, to a socket that may otherwise read it, is `organization_closed`, which is not final: a reopen admits the same credential again.

methods.name: sessions.about
methods.description: What the organization holds of the sessions `ids` names (`Gentility.Sessions.about/2`), at most 200 an ask: each one's `status`, `archived_at` and `last_server_seq`, archived ones included, for a desk placing rows `sessions.list` does not carry. An id the organization does not hold, or one that is not a UUID, is left out rather than refused.

schema.description: Session ids.

methods.name: sessions.archive
methods.description: Archives a session this desk never held (`Gentility.Sessions.archive/3`): the server writes `archived_at` through the inbox and answers when. One already archived comes back as it stands. `archived_at` is null only where a later inbox write already holds the row unarchived.

schema.description: The session's id.

methods.name: sessions.ask
methods.description: Raises an ask about one session of the Desk that holds it, for a person's window (`Gentility.Desk.SessionAsk.raise_for_window/5`), and waits up to 20 s for the answer. `kind` is `session_stop`, `session_answer`, `session_resume`, `session_manage` (`close` only) or `session_tags`, raised of the lease holder, or `session_start`, raised of `host`; any other is `bad_kind`. The answer is the ask as it stands: `pending`, `expired`, or `decided` with the Desk's `decision` and `result`. A start of a session already open answers `opened` with its row and raises nothing.

schema.description: The kind's (`machine.ask`'s `x-kinds`), less what the server adds; `by` only where an agent asks.
The machine a `session_start` is raised of.

decision.description: With `decided` only, and always: the Desk's word.

result.description: With `decided` only, and always: the text the Desk's answer gave under its kind's keys (`Gentility.Desk.AskKinds.result/2`).

session.description: With `opened` only, and always: the session's feed row.

methods.name: sessions.ask_read
methods.description: An ask this person raised in this organization, as it stands (`Gentility.Desk.SessionAsk.read/2`), expired first when it is due: `pending`, `expired`, or `decided` with its `decision` and `result`. `result` is null for an ask answered before answers kept their words. Anyone else's ask is `not_found`.

decision.description: With `decided` only, and always: the Desk's word.

result.description: With `decided` only, and always: the text the Desk's answer gave under its kind's keys (`Gentility.Desk.AskKinds.result/2`).

session.description: With `opened` only, and always: the session's feed row.

methods.name: sessions.brief_bind
methods.description: Bind or upgrade a session brief through Briefs.Binding. Project is a slug; absent inherits the existing binding context. Grants.authorize validates agent attribution. expected_revision_id fences a change; a matching requested revision and context succeeds on retry. Requires thread_briefs.

methods.name: sessions.facts
methods.description: One page of a session's whole run log, every origin, after `after_seq` (`Gentility.Sessions.facts/5`), for a desk rehoming it: at most `limit` facts, a larger one clamped to 500, and `more` when the log holds more. Only the session's owner reads it, and their agent needs a current management grant. A `turn_body` fact comes with its stored `items` inlined. An optional actor is checked for a bound host (a live member who may operate the session and owns it) and ignored for a person. An actor refusal is `forbidden`.

schema.description: A seq; 0, the beginning, when absent.
Positive; 500 when absent.
The person a bound host acts for.

client_seq.description: Null for a fact the server minted.

payload.description: The fact's own, as the log holds it: each event type's keys.

methods.name: sessions.feed
methods.description: The organization's session feed since the reader's cursor (`Gentility.Sessions.Feed.page/4`): rows, holders, the grants the reader may see (a grant a thread passed on only to a reader whose hello says `delegated_grants`), the reader's own read marks and the ids gone, stamped past `since`, at most `limit` of them all in stamp order. `cursor` is where to ask from next, and `more` says there is more past it. A `since` past the server's cursor or behind its pruned removals, or a `generation` that is not the reader's, answers an empty page with `reset`: the reader starts again from zero.

schema.description: The reader's cursor; 0 when absent.
The generation the reader's cursor was kept with; null or absent for none.
1 to 500; 200 when absent.

machine.description: Null for the server's own hold.

label.description: The machine's label; null for the server.

granted_at.description: Null for a grant revoked before it was ever given.

by_session_id.description: The thread that passed this grant on (T-584); null for the person's own. Sent only to a reader whose hello says `delegated_grants`.

basis_scope.description: The scope of the person's grant to `by_session_id` this one rests on; null for the person's own.

basis_granted_at.description: That grant's `granted_at`: this one stands only while that decision does.

read_at.description: Null for a row marked unread.

gone.description: Ids of sessions removed from the feed.

methods.name: sessions.find
methods.description: The organization's sessions every breadcrumb given points at (`Gentility.Sessions.Finder.find/3`), newest activity first, at most `limit` (20 when absent, at most 100). At least one breadcrumb is needed (`no_breadcrumb`). Each session says why it matched and where it was worked. The socket's machine goes with the ask, so a session's own machine reads its paths back.

schema.description: Words in a title, a former title or a prompt.
A file the session touched, or a directory above it.
7 to 64 hex digits of a commit.
A GitHub pull request's URL, or `{repo, number}`.
`owner/name` or a remote URL.
An ISO 8601 instant or date: last active at or after it.
An ISO 8601 instant or date: opened at or before it.
A machine's id or its label.

former_titles.description: Its titles before this one, oldest first.

recap_line.description: Null where the session has none, or its recap is not the reader's to see.

recap_hidden.description: Whether a recap is withheld from this reader (`Gentility.Sessions.published_recaps/2`).

repository.description: `owner/name` where the session names a GitHub repository, else its remote as given; null for none.

branches.description: Its places' branches, each once, in the order first seen.

machine.description: The machine's label; null where the machine is gone.

worktree_path.description: Only to the session's owner, or a desk asking from that machine; null to anyone else.

pull_request.description: The session's current pull request, or null for none.

prompt.description: Its first prompt, cut to 600 characters; null for none.

url.description: The session's page on the server.

commits_matched.description: With a `sha` only: the commits it matched; else empty.

paths_matched.description: With a `path` only: the files it matched; else empty.

reason.description: One clause for each breadcrumb that matched, joined by `; `.

methods.name: sessions.heard
methods.description: One page of what a session's pull requests heard (`Gentility.Sessions.PullRequestHearing.heard_since/3`): each `pr_heard` payload with `at` and `seq`, in log order, at most 100, and `more` when the log holds more. `after_seq` starts after that seq; `after`, an ISO 8601 instant, starts at it and may repeat what a desk holds; neither starts at the beginning, and both is `malformed_payload`.

items.description: A `pr_heard` as the log holds it. A kind writes its own keys beside these, and a fact keeps the ones its kind wrote when it was heard: `run_attempt` and `conclusion` on a failed run, `branch` on a failed run on a merge commit, `state` on a review, `path` on a review comment or a resolved thread, `failed` and `runs` on `merge_checks_done`.

key.description: What makes it once per session.

excerpt.description: A third party's words, at most 2,000 characters.

methods.name: sessions.lease_take
methods.description: Moves a session's lease to the machine `to`, from the epoch the asker holds (`Gentility.Sessions.Inbox.take_lease/5`), from Desk only: the answer is the new holder and epoch. An epoch that has moved on is `stale_epoch`, with the epoch the server holds. A bound host names the person it acts for in `actor`.

schema.description: The machine to hold it.
The person a bound host acts for.

methods.name: sessions.list
methods.description: The organization's sessions as rows, with the server's `now` for the reader's clocks. `since` (an ISO 8601 instant, or null for everything) keeps the rows changed after it, archived ones included, so a reader catches up on what it missed. Otherwise `include_archived` says whether archived rows come too.

methods.name: sessions.locate
methods.description: A thread found from a person's words (`Gentility.Sessions.Find.ask/2`): one paid `thread_find` run, answered inside 27 s, whose picks are re-read as the asker, so a session the asker may not read is dropped. A socket has at most two at once; past that it is `unavailable`. An ok reply's `status` is the run's own: it may be `failed` with non-empty `picks` when the run wound down on its budget after answering, and the picks are still the answer. The refusal `failed` is a run with nothing to show.

schema.description: At most 2,000 characters, not blank.

model.description: Null where the run never named one.

former_titles.description: Its titles before this one, oldest first.

recap_line.description: Null where the session has none, or its recap is not the reader's to see.

recap_hidden.description: Whether a recap is withheld from this reader (`Gentility.Sessions.published_recaps/2`).

repository.description: `owner/name` where the session names a GitHub repository, else its remote as given; null for none.

branches.description: Its places' branches, each once, in the order first seen.

machine.description: The machine's label; null where the machine is gone.

worktree_path.description: Only to the session's owner, or a desk asking from that machine; null to anyone else.

pull_request.description: The session's current pull request, or null for none.

prompt.description: Its first prompt, cut to 600 characters; null for none.

url.description: The session's page on the server.

reason.description: The model's one sentence, plain text.

methods.name: sessions.open
methods.description: Opens a session for the socket's machine to hold (`Gentility.Sessions.open/2`), from Desk only, minting its lease. A repeated open of the person's own session answers it as it stands. The answer names the session, the `client_seq` it holds, `accepts` (what a batch may carry: `internal`), the lease's holder and its epoch. The machine is the socket's, never the payload's. A bound host names the person it opens for in `actor`; a session another machine holds is `held_elsewhere`, with that machine and epoch.

schema.description: A UUID the desk minted; the server mints one when absent.
The person a bound host acts for.
An ISO 8601 instant: when the desk opened it.
The agent that opened it, 1 to 200 characters.
The session and turn a fork continues.
A looper's fork: the looper, believed only as `ask_id`'s.
A looper's fork: the `session_fork` ask it answers.

machine.description: The socket's machine; null for a socket that named none.

methods.name: sessions.transcript
methods.description: Read the server's indexed copy for the authenticated person. Bound hosts are refused. Four concurrent reads per RPC connection; at most 100 turns and 8 MiB per answer.

methods.name: sessions.unarchive
methods.description: Puts an archived session back, from any desk, held or not (`Gentility.Sessions.unarchive/3`): the fact is the server's alone. One not archived comes back as it stands. `archived_at` is null but where a later inbox write already holds the row archived.

methods.name: sessions.write
methods.description: Words the organization's model writes for a session (`Gentility.Sessions.Writing.write/5`): a `kind` from a closed list and its `inputs`, never a prompt. `session_name` writes `title` and `branch`; `session_recap` writes `recap`, `line`, `waiting_on` and `title`; each is null where the model gave nothing usable. A socket has at most four in flight; past that, and on any failure once the inputs are read, it is `unavailable`.

schema.description: `session_name` or `session_recap`; any other is `unknown_kind`.
The kind's: `prompt` and `project` for `session_name`; `transcript`, `previous`, `title` and `pull_request` for `session_recap`.

object.description: `branch` with `session_name` only, and always; `recap`, `line` and `waiting_on` with `session_recap` only, and always.

methods.name: sessions.written
methods.description: One page of what the server wrote on a session itself (`Gentility.Sessions.Written.since/4`): every fact with no `client_seq` that is not internal, after `after_seq` or from the beginning, at most 100, and `more` when the log holds more. Only the session's owner, or a desk on the machine it was last seen on, reads it.

payload.description: The fact's own, as the log holds it: each event type's keys.

x-notifications.name: groups.changed
x-notifications.description: A group of the organization changed: an append to its ledger (`agent_groups`). It carries the group's id and nothing of its words, so a core reads the group, or the list, again. Heard after an `rpc.watch` of `groups`, served only on `/desk/rpc`.

x-notifications.name: lobby.hosts_changed
x-notifications.description: Something `lobby.desk_hosts` reads moved, or a node's presence did (`Gentility.Desk.Hints`): the desk asks again. The payload is empty. The server says it to a socket whose server advertises `reach_hints`.

x-notifications.name: lobby.projects_changed
x-notifications.description: A project was created, renamed or archived, or had a repository attached or detached: the desk asks `projects.list` again. Not `changed`, which a released core reads as a session-feed hint. The payload is empty: no cursor, since nothing reads one.

x-notifications.name: lobby.refusals_changed
x-notifications.description: The refusal list moved in a way a person sees (`Gentility.Desk.Hints.refusals_changed/1`): a new edge or reason, a mute or unmute, the sweep, a reach grant. A burst is said at most once every ten seconds a socket, the first at once and the rest as one when the quiet ends. The payload is empty, and the desk asks `refusals.list` again.

x-notifications.name: loopers.changed
x-notifications.description: The board moved: `{scope: "runs", cursor}` to every reader, `{scope: "loopers", cursor, user_id}` to the owner whose loopers moved. A desk with `looper_feed` pulls `loopers.feed` past its cursor; an older one lists again.

x-notifications.name: machine.ask
x-notifications.description: A command for the machine, at least once and idempotent on `id`: pushed after every join, and again when raised. `payload` is its kind's, and `x-kinds` says each kind's payload, the `decisions` an answer may settle it with and the `refusals` the core may give, as `Gentility.Desk.AskKinds` declares them. A kind is answered with an `ask_answered` fact on `machine.fact`, but `phone_claim`, answered on `machine.answer`. `x-answer`'s `refusals` are the core's own reasons for refusing an ask of any kind (`Desk.AskKinds.own_refusals/0`).

schema.description: Open: a core answers a kind it does not read `unsupported`, once (`a_kind_this_build_does_not_read_is_recorded_and_reads_as_unsupported`, `desk/core/src/reactors/asks.rs`), and only a core reads asks. A kind a released core would misread still waits for a hello word.
Its kind's: `x-kinds`.
An ISO 8601 instant.

payload.description: An approval carries `request_id` and `option_id`; a question's answer `question_id`, `action` and, with an `accept`, `value`; never keys of both. A core reads a question's answer with no key beside its own (`QuestionAnswerAsk`, `deny_unknown_fields`).

value.description: The typed answer, with an `accept` only.

repository.description: An `owner/name`, lowercased; exactly one of `repository` and `cwd` is not null.

prompt.description: Absent on a start without a prompt, raised only of a core whose hello said `start_without_prompt`.

id.description: The message id the sender's core minted; the same id on its `message_sent` and the recipient's `message_requested`.

from_mode.description: The sender's permission mode in Desk's words, from its own core; absent ranks as supervised.

sender.description: The server's voucher for the sender, which the holder may not hold: the sending thread, or, with `kind` `group`, a group of threads (T-622), raised only of a core whose hello says `group_message`. A group's message is asked by its person (`by` has no `session_id`) and has no address to reply to.

kind.description: Absent for a thread, as before groups; `group` for a group, whose `id` is the group's and names no session.

manager.description: The server's voucher for a manager the holder may not hold; null with `manager_id`.

opened_ask.description: Only on the server's own stamp of a thread a coordinator opened (T-200): the start ask's id.

x-notifications.name: rpc.revoked
x-notifications.description: What the connection proved has stopped proving it (`Gentility.Accounts.Revocations`). `scope: "org"` names one organization the person no longer reaches, and calls naming it are refused `forbidden`; `scope: "connection"` is the credential itself, and the server closes with 4401 (`credential_revoked`, or `revoked` for a host whose binding was revoked on purpose) or 4409 (`superseded`, after which a host stops reconnecting); a released core stops dialling `/desk/rpc` on either.

schema.description: Why, for the log and the person. Open: reasons will grow (an unbound machine, a deleted organization), so a reader acts on `scope` alone and keeps a reason it does not know.

x-notifications.name: sessions.changed
x-notifications.description: The session feed moved (`Gentility.Sessions.Feed`): `{scope: "sessions", cursor}` to every reader; `{scope: "reads", cursor, user_id}` to that reader alone; `{scope: "written", cursor, machine_id}` when only a row's server cursor moved, naming the machine holding it; `{scope: "grants", cursor, user_id}` to a socket that reads that person's grants; `{scope: "grants", cursor, scope_changed: true}` to a bound host. A desk with the feed pulls `sessions.feed` past its cursor.

schema.description: `sessions`, `reads`, `written` or `grants`.
Null for a row no desk holds.

Asker.description: Who asked: a person's `id` and `name`, and the asking thread's `session_id` when an agent inside a Desk thread asked, or a grant let one speak for the person; `delegated_by` names the thread whose grant it acts on, when one was passed on (T-584). Automatic updates ask as `{id: "automatic-updates", name: "Automatic updates"}`.

delegated_by.description: When the asking thread acts on a grant another thread passed on (T-584), that thread's id.

DeskHello.description: A core's hello (`GentilityWeb.DeskHello`): logged and never refused. At most 64 feature words of 1 to 128 printable characters.

FeedRow.description: One session as the lobby's `feed` gives it (`Gentility.Sessions.Feed.Row.build/2`): the row's own evidence, stamped with `row_seq` and the fold version. A row's recorded form is its difference from `rows/feed.json`. `attention_line`, `waiting_on` and `waiting_reason` are the reader's own rows' alone.

last_closed_at.description: The latest time the session was closed, which a reopen leaves standing; null when never. A grant the session passed on ends at it (T-584).

last_archived_at.description: The latest time the session was archived, which a unarchive leaves standing; null when never. A grant the session passed on ends at it (T-584).

Group.description: A group as a person reads it (`Gentility.AgentGroups.read/3` with `header: true`): its question, its members and their state, a page of its posts, and the Desk window header's progress in words and convened time.

status.description: `running`, `summarising` (its chair writes the closing summary) or `ended`.

turns.description: Round robin's turns; null in another style.

max_posts.description: Freeform's post limit; null in another style.

ends_at.description: When a freeform group ends; null in another style.

chair.description: The chair's label, or null for no chair.

session_id.description: The member's thread, minted at convene.

state.description: Its state in words, lower case: `answering`, `waiting`, `passed`, `missed its turn`, `not started`, `done`. Open: words may be added.

started.description: Whether the member's thread ever started: false for one whose start failed, which has no thread to open.

posts.description: Up to 50 posts after `after`, oldest first.

kind.description: `answer`, or `summary` for the chair's closing summary.

round.description: Its round, in together and round robin; null in freeform.

hidden.description: Posts hidden from a member thread during an open together round; a person sees every post, so 0.

summary.description: Whether the chair posted a closing summary.

end_message_failed.description: Why the end message could not reach the convening thread, or null.

progress.description: The group's progress in words, for the Desk window's header, as the web's page words it: `Starting`, `Round 1`, `Turn 3 of 8`, `12 of 20 posts`, `Summarising`, `Waiting for C's summary because …` or `Ended because …`. Shown word for word.

convened_at.description: When the group was convened, ISO 8601, for the Desk window's header.

GroupRow.description: One group as `groups.list` lists it (`Gentility.AgentGroups.list/2`), from the projections.

status.description: `running`, `summarising` (its chair writes the closing summary) or `ended`.

answer_count.description: The members' answers, the chair's summary not counted.

convened_by.description: Who convened it, as the convening fact's actor snapshot names them.

LooperChat.description: What the reader may do with a run's reply composer now (`Gentility.CloudLoop.Chat.run_state/2`), and the server's sentence for why not (`GentilityWeb.LooperChat`). `reason` is one of `looper_say`'s refusal words; `busy_run` names the run holding the looper's slot when it is `looper_busy`, and `forked_to` the thread a forked run carried on in.

LooperModel.description: A run's or looper's model (`LoopSerializer.serialize_assoc_model/1`), or null when none is loaded. `display_name` is null until the catalog knows it.

LooperRef.description: The looper a run row names: the same id an `OwnedLooper` carries, so a desk hangs a run under its pin by one id. `responder` is whether the looper has a trigger binding.

LooperRequest.description: One request a run raised (`CloudLoop.Requests.Serializer.serialize/3`). `can_resolve` and `can_grant` are the reader's. A request on a `loopers.feed` row carries no `can_grant` or `missing`: both read the organization's integrations and secrets, which no board digest covers.

requested.description: The narrowable fields at the values the agent asked for, by key.

LooperRun.description: One run read whole: the row's fields less its requests, and the run page's header (`LoopSerializer.serialize_loop/2`). `result_text` is null where the reader may not see the run's last word, and `result_hidden` says so.

LooperRunRow.description: One run on the board (`LooperThreadsChannel.row/5`): what a sidebar row and its drawer need, with its open requests.

LooperWake.description: Why a run woke: the wake's reason and source, its hop, the event that caused it, and the task it ran for.

OwnedLooper.description: One looper the reader owns, as a desk pins it (`LooperThreadsChannel.owned/2`).

platform.description: `ios` or `android`; null until the phone's first `register`, since the claim poll writes the row.

has_push.description: Whether the server holds a push token for it.

PullRequestSpoken.description: What a session's words on its pull request were given (`Gentility.Sessions.PullRequestSpeech.speak/5`): the pull request, GitHub's address for them, and GitHub's ids as the `pr_commented` fact records them. A comment has a `comment_id` and no `review_id`, a review a `review_id` and no `comment_id`, and a reply both, its `review_id` null when GitHub filed it under none.

url.description: GitHub's address for what was posted.

QuestionAnswer.description: An addressed question's recorded answer, as `Gentility.Sessions.Questions.Commands` reads it off the `question_answered` fact.

action.description: `accept`, `decline` or `cancel`, or a word a newer writer said.

value.description: The answer to the question's form: an object, or null for a decline. The person's, so open.

answered_by.description: Who answered, as the fact names them; null where it names nobody.

Refusal.description: A refusal's words: the closed `reason` and, where a person reads it, a `message`. `malformed_payload` and `unknown_event` name the `event` they answered; `malformed_batch` names the `index` of the first fact it refused. `session.append`'s refusals carry the detail the core acts on, each property naming its word.

ask_id.description: RPC sessions.ask: task_died includes this only after a serialized recovery found the committed ask. outcome_unknown always includes the connection-minted id, whose commit could not be confirmed. Read with sessions.ask_read; not_found after outcome_unknown is still uncertain.

event_type.description: `server_only_event`: the fact type only the server writes.

item.description: `unknown_message` and `invalid_role`, of `session.append`: the transcript item the server's copy could not place, by its `id` and `kind` and never its content. Optional: a core that reads it says which item stalls the thread.

actor.description: `unknown_actor`: the actor named who is not a member of the session's organization; null where a bound host named none (`sessions.lease_take`).

epoch.description: `stale_epoch`: the lease epoch the server holds, null for a session no machine holds. `held_elsewhere`: the epoch of the hold that refused the open.

answer.description: `already_decided`, of `question_answer` and `question_dismiss`: the answer already recorded, where the server holds one.

errors.description: `invalid`, as `GentilityWeb.ChannelRefusal.refusal/1` writes it from a changeset (`models_seen` among them): each field the changeset refused, and its sentences. `malformed_payload`, of `question_answer`: one sentence for each field of the answer that does not fit the question's form, by field.

detail.description: `failed` (`sessions.locate`): why the run had nothing to show, in the run's own word.

machine.description: `held_elsewhere` (`sessions.open`): the machine that holds the session, null where none does.

topic.description: `event_emit_failed`: the event topic whose emit failed.

RpcOrganization.description: An organization the connection's credential reaches: a person's every live membership with MCP access, a bound host's machine's one.

SessionPullRequest.description: A session's current pull request, or null for none (`summary/8`'s and `Feed.Row`'s `pull_request/1`). `head` is the branch it was opened from, null for a row folded before that column; `draft`, `checks` and `review` are the current link's.

SessionPullRequestLink.description: One pull request a session is linked to and has not unlinked (`link/1`), in the order first linked. `heard_at` is when the session last heard of it.

SessionTags.description: A thread's tags as one reader reads them (`Gentility.Sessions.Tags.for_sessions/1`): `manager` and `started_by` name a thread of the same organization or are null, `managing` the threads it manages.

TranscriptCompaction.description: A compaction anchored at a turn, failed ones included. `summary` is null past the private boundary, and `summary_hidden` says so.

TranscriptStep.description: The model step a turn was, or null.

TranscriptToolCall.description: One tool call of a turn. `arguments` and `result` are any JSON, redacted past the private boundary.

children.description: A sub-agent's calls, each in this shape, and a sandboxed call's own calls, in a smaller one (`id`, `name`, `status`, `arguments`, `result`, the two `_redacted` flags and `private`). Open until the children are typed.

TranscriptTurn.description: One turn of a run (`Transcripts.Serializer.turns/2`). `content` and `reasoning` are null on a turn past the reader's private boundary, and `private` says so.

author.description: Who typed the row, on a row a person typed (T-713): their id, and their name, null for a user who is gone. Absent on every other row.

TranscriptUsage.description: A turn's usage, or null. `cost` is a decimal string. `estimated` is present, and true, only where the row was estimated.

WorkSessionRow.description: One session as the lobby's `list` gives it (`WorkSessionsChannel.summary/8`). A row's recorded form is its difference from `rows/work_session.json`. `attention_line`, `waiting_on` and `waiting_reason` are the reader's own rows' alone; `recap` is null when withheld (`recap_hidden`).

x-rpc.description: The same methods as JSON-RPC 2.0 over one WebSocket (plan 2026-11-08, section 3). A method without `x-phoenix` is served there only. Auth is at the upgrade, `Authorization: Bearer <token>` or `Authorization: Desk-Host <credential>`, refused with a 403 whose JSON body names the word. `rpc.hello` is the first request. A domain in `scope` takes that field beside its params, and its notifications carry it, except `person`: phone methods act as the authenticated person with no scope parameter, rechecking liveness on every call and refusing bound hosts; a `machine` method acts for the machine the connection's hello named; a `session` method writes the session its `session` names, passing that session's door on every call as a join of `work_session:<session>` did once, and a session not there or not this connection's to write is `forbidden`, and one of a closed organization, or an `org` that is closed, is `organization_closed`, which a core asks again after; the server serves a domain once it advertises `rpc_<domain>`, the word `features` names by method-name domain; a deprecated method is not served here. A refusal is an `error` whose `data` is the refusal as the Phoenix framing answers it (`reason`, and `message` or `event` where it has them) and whose `code` is by its word.
x-rpc.org: An `org` field, in params and in notifications, is the organization's id (`RpcOrganization.id`), never its slug.
x-rpc.person: The phone domain has param-less person scope: the connection's authenticated person. No user_id or org selector is required or used. Each call rechecks credential liveness; a bound host is forbidden.

codes.-32603: RPC-only task failure: sessions.ask task_died after serialized recovery or outcome_unknown if recovery failed; pulls writes outcome_unknown when a task dies and GitHub may have acted; questions writes outcome_unknown when a task dies and the question may have changed; models and MCP writes outcome_unknown when a task dies after it may have changed state; groups writes outcome_unknown when a convene or a stop task dies after it may have acted

close.1009: message_too_big: a frame past `max_frame` bytes, which the server cannot read, so it closes the connection and every domain on it. A core never sends one: it refuses a request past `max_frame` itself, unsent
close.1012: restart: the server is draining for a deploy; reconnect with backoff. Best-effort: behind kamal-proxy a deploy usually shows as 1006, the connection cut with no close frame, because the proxy cuts upgraded connections at its switch, before the old node stops and drains. A core reads 1006 exactly as 1012
close.1013: organization_closed: a host's hello met an organization closed since the upgrade. The hello is not answered, so a core reads the close as a dropped transport and reconnects with backoff; the upgrade then refuses it 403 `organization_closed`, which it also reconnects after, so a reopen lets it back in with the same credential
close.4401: credential_revoked: the credential is dead. A person's Desk logs in again, and a host is bound again, before reconnecting; neither retries the same credential. A host whose binding was revoked on purpose is closed with it too, its word `revoked`, at once if it is connected and at once after the upgrade if it dials again. A released core stops dialling `/desk/rpc` on 4401; its Phoenix socket stops reconnecting only on `superseded`, so it goes on dialling `/socket` with backoff and is refused 403 `revoked` each time
close.4403: organization_closed: the organization the connection acts for was closed. Not final: the credential is untouched, so a core dials again with backoff, is refused at the upgrade 403 `organization_closed` while it stays closed, and is let in with the same credential once it is reopened
